task: RoboCasa GR1 tabletop PnPMilkToMicrowaveClose (Fourier GR1, arms+waist+hands, 29-DoF action), 20 seeds (0-19) x 720 sim steps, 20 Hz control, 16-step action chunks, 4 denoise steps
policy: youliangtan/gr00t-n1.5-robocasa-tabletop-posttrain @ b46fb3c (GR00T N1.5 post-trained on the RoboCasa tabletop tasks); PyTorch (not TensorRT) on every backend
pairing: one diffusion-noise bank (seed 5000, 20x50x1x16x32 fp32) injected bit-identically into every backend; scenes deep-reseeded per seed; per-(episode, call) noise pairing

fp8_isolation_same_board.reading: Thor fp8's flips vs the 5090 decompose into one hardware/stack flip (seed 7, which also flips under Thor bf16) and two fp8-precision flips (seeds 8 and 10).

fp8_engagement_proof.backend: torch-native float8_e4m3fn via torch._scaled_mm (per-tensor dynamic-act + static-weight scales, E4M3)

fp8_engagement_accounting: 664,200 e4m3 GEMMs / 900 policy calls = 738 per call = 165 (SigLIP) + 84 (Qwen LLM, select_layer 12) + 1 (mlp1) + 24 (VL self-attn) + 4 x 116 (DiT per Euler step). Attention, norms, patch-embed and the per-embodiment state/action encoder+decoder stay bf16.
latency_note: closed-loop latencies are PyTorch eager policy calls (not TensorRT): board compute, and in-loop incl. host<->board ZMQ. On Thor, fp8 is slower than bf16 at batch 1 (dynamic-quantisation overhead): in-loop incl. ZMQ ~141 vs ~76 ms; board compute in the table. Use results/speed for deployable latency.
caveats: The 5090 reference is bf16, not fp32 ground truth.

n = 20 seeds, one noise draw per seed: Wilson 95% CIs are about +/-20 points and overlap for every backend (all ~40-50%). The data rule out a collapse, not a 10-20 point degradation; the fp8 > bf16 rate ordering is noise.
The checkpoint authors report 0.60 for this task (SOURCED: Isaac-GR00T examples/RoboCasa/README.md at the pinned commit); our 45% (Wilson CI 26-66%) is consistent with it.

Seed 14's initial observation is nondeterministic on the host simulator (3 distinct call-0 hashes over 7 host sweeps; not the seeded layout RNG). It is a win on every backend and in no flip; excluding it leaves the conclusions unchanged (Orin 8/19 = 5090 8/19; Thor fp8 9/19 vs 8/19).

The 5090 reference run predates call-0 hashing, so its scene identity is inferred (host probe + call-0 action agreement <=0.013 vs ~0.30 for a different scene). The 2026-09-18 board runs hash-match each other on 19/20 seeds (all but 14); the 2026-10-12 Thor bf16 re-run also differs at seed 5, which is not a flip seed.
Thor fp8 determinism was not tested (no repeat run); Orin fp16 is bit-exact across two processes.
Thor fp8's flips are heterogeneous: seed 8 is a true boundary case; seed 10 is a large-divergence success (per-call rel_mae peaks at 1.70) that won the seed the 5090 lost.
reproduce: accuracy/run_closed_loop.py per backend, then accuracy/finalize.py and accuracy/make_summary.py (docs/ACCURACY.md)
